name: Modbus Controller Output
description: The `modbus_controller` platform creates an output from a modbus_controller. The goal is to write a value to a modbus register on a device.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: start address of the first register in a range (can be decimal or hexadecimal).

config_entries.label: Inverted
config_entries.description: If the output should be treated as inverted. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Power Supply
config_entries.description: The [power supply](https://esphome.io/components/power_supply/) to connect to this output. When the output is enabled, the power supply will automatically be switched on too.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Bitmask
config_entries.description: sometimes multiple values are packed in a single register's response. The bitmask is used to determined if the result is true or false. See [Bitmasks](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller#bitmasks).

config_entries.label: Custom Pdu
config_entries.description: The modbus PDU (function code + data) for a custom command. This allows using non-standard commands. The device address (taken from the controller's `address:`) and the CRC are added automatically, so do not include a leading device-address byte. If `custom_pdu` is used, `address` and `register_type` can't be used. Renamed from `custom_command`, which is now removed and raises a config-validation error. See [Using `custom_pdu`](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller/#modbus_custom_pdu) for how to use `custom_pdu`.

config_entries.label: Expect Broadcast Write Response
config_entries.description: When the controller's `address` is `0` (see `allow_broadcast_read` on [Modbus Controller](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller/)), wait for the reply to each write instead of treating it as a fire-and-forget broadcast. Rejected under a controller at any other address. Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Lambda
config_entries.description: Lambda to be evaluated every update interval to get the new value of the binary sensor. Parameters: Possible return values for the lambda:

config_entries.label: Max Power
config_entries.description: Sets the maximum output value of this output platform. Must be in range from min_power to 1. Defaults to `1`.

config_entries.label: Min Power
config_entries.description: Sets the minimum output value of this output platform. Must be in range from 0 to max_power. Defaults to `0`. If zero_means_zero is `false` this will be output value when the entity is turned off.

config_entries.label: Multiply
config_entries.description: multiply the incoming value with this factor before writing it to the device. Ignored if `write_lambda` is defined. Only valid for `register_type: holding`.

config_entries.label: Offset
config_entries.description: Offset from start address in bytes (only required for uncommon response encodings). If more than one register is written in a command this value is used to find the start of this datapoint relative to start address. The component calculates the size of the range based on offset and size of the value type.

config_entries.label: Response Size
config_entries.description: Number of bytes the poll reads to cover this binary sensor. For the register types (`holding`/`read`) it defaults to `2` (one register); raise it only when the bit you are reading sits in a wider response, such as a `custom_pdu` reply spanning several registers. It sets the size of the read, not which bit is published — the bit is always selected by `offset` and `bitmask`. It has no effect on the `coil` and `discrete_input` types, which are always read as a single bit.

config_entries.label: Reuse Previous Range
config_entries.description: How this item relates to the register range built just before it (same register type, ascending address order). `auto` (default) joins when the addresses are adjacent and the item's position in the reply is exact; `true` joins unconditionally, reading across address gaps and past registers with a non-standard `response_size`; `false` always starts a new range here (later items may still extend it). See [Register ranges](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller/#modbus_register_count). Replaces the deprecated `force_new_range` and `register_count` options, which will be removed in 2027.3.0 — the linked section covers migration.

config_entries.label: Skip Updates
config_entries.description: **Deprecated and no longer has any effect** — every register range is polled on each `update_interval`. The key is still accepted (logging a config-time warning) and will be removed in 2027.3.0. To poll some registers less often, place those sensors on a second `modbus_controller` with the same `address:` and a slower `update_interval:`.

config_entries.label: Use Write Multiple
config_entries.description: By default the modbus command *Function Code 6 (Preset Single Registers)* is used for setting the holding register if only one register is set. If your device only supports *Function Code 16 (Preset Multiple Registers)* set this option to `true`.

config_entries.label: Value Type
config_entries.description: data type of the modbus register data. The default data type for modbus is a 16 bit integer in big endian format (MSB first). This option applies only to `register_type: holding`; it is not a valid option with `register_type: coil`.

options.label: U_WORD_S
options.description: unsigned 16 bit integer from 1 register with bytes swapped within the register = 16bit

options.label: S_WORD_S
options.description: signed 16 bit integer from 1 register with bytes swapped within the register = 16bit

options.label: U_DWORD_R
options.description: unsigned 32 bit integer from 2 registers low word first

options.label: S_DWORD_R
options.description: signed 32 bit integer from 2 registers low word first

options.label: U_QWORD_R
options.description: unsigned 64 bit integer from 4 registers low word first

options.label: S_QWORD_R
options.description: signed 64 bit integer from 4 registers low word first

options.label: FP32
options.description: 32 bit IEEE 754 floating point from 2 registers

options.label: FP32_R
options.description: 32 bit IEEE 754 floating point - same as FP32 but low word first

config_entries.label: Write Lambda
config_entries.description: Lambda is evaluated before the modbus write command is created. The value is passed in as `float x` (or `bool x` for `register_type: coil`). Parameters passed into the lambda Possible return values for the lambda:

config_entries.label: Zero Means Zero
config_entries.description: Sets the output to use actual 0 instead of `min_power`. Defaults to `false`.
